name: Onboarding design changes
description:
Onboarding should be a single flow.

- If the user only has one board, skip "Choose board for this introduction" and assume that one board.
- There should be tabs at the top to indicate which step you are in onboarding, allow the user to click in these tabs to go forwards / backwards.
- At the software factory step, remove the "Choose agent skills" option as the user has already passed that. That screen should be titled "Stage Prompts" with an introduction to how they work. Then give 3 options to the user: "Populate stage prompts with default prompts", "Populate stage prompts with minimal prompts". Default prompts should be described as pre-built instructions generated by the Rowbly team, minimal prompts are described as minimal placeholders the user should edit later.

The steps for onboarding should be as follows:
- "How will you use this data root"
- Choose board (skip if only one board)
- Setup plugins
- Setup agent skills
- Setup stage prompts
- Final step, summary of selection + "Finish onboarding"

comments.author: sunny
comments.body: User decision: use the combined ROW-86 flow. Remove the AI usage question; combine Factory setup and Stage Prompts into one Stage Prompts step with default prompts, minimal prompts and Edit Stage Prompts options; show Plugins in all modes; tabs are Usage, Board (skip when exactly one Board), Plugins, Agent skills, Stage Prompts (Software Factory or Both), Summary. Retain ROW-77 saved onboardingSteps progress, freely clickable tabs, Back/Next/Skip controls, Next without completeness gating, completion marks and inline results. This supersedes conflicting earlier details; ROW-77, ROW-78 and ROW-80 are now merged, so ROW-86 is a follow-up on main. Minimal prompts use the existing placeholder template text and are off by default; setup accepts default|minimal prompts. Do not reintroduce forward-only tabs or apply-on-Finish behavior.
